journal: Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Process Design and Development 23, 533-538
title: Solubility of Methane in Brines From 0 to 300 C
experimental_method: Gas extraction: methane dissolved in brine in a high-pressure heated/cooled stirred reactor (to 13.2 MPa); 4-8 methane-saturated liquid samples per condition cooled to room temperature and degassed into a constant-temperature gas buret for PVT measurement of vapour and residual dissolved methane (Cramer 1980). Reagent-grade salts in demineralized water.
uncertainties_stated: Experimental error in the modified Henry's law constant 5.8 % (worst-case analysis of measurement errors, Cramer 1980). Relative standard errors of the smoothing fit (Table IV) 5.1-10.5 %.
quality_remarks: Results are printed only as mean modified Henry's law constants k (MPa) with total reactor pressure; mole fractions are not printed, and k uses the author's computed methane partial pressure and a chart fugacity coefficient. Six water-block values (footnote b) are recomputed from Culberson and McKetta (1951), not measured here (held). Some rows show large scatter (NaCl-3 at 203.7 C 7430 vs 205.3 C 10870; NaCl-4 112.6 C 21110 vs 115.7 C 27470). The abstract and text say measurements 0-300 C; lowest printed T is 0.5 C. Paper is printed directly after another article (pages 533 top: end of a previous paper's references) and before Fan et al. on p. 538; tables checked to belong to this paper. Temperature scale not stated.
